title: White Grub: How to Spot It and Stop It in Your Mais and Palay
metaTitle: White Grub: Root Damage and Control in the Philippines
metaDescription: The white grub eats roots and leaves corn and sugarcane yellow and wilted. Learn its signs, its season and the control steps that work.
excerpt: The white grub, Leucopholis irrorata, is the fat, curled larva of a chafer beetle that eats roots underground. You see yellow, wilting and dying plants, and you find the grubs when you dig. This page shows the signs and the steps that cut the number of beetles and grubs.

heroImage.alt: An adult Leucopholis irrorata beetle, the parent of the white grubs that eat corn and sugarcane roots
heroImage.credit: Forest Botial Jarvis, CC BY, via iNaturalist

blocks.text:
The white grub is also called the root grub. In the Philippines it is one of the four major insect pests of corn, and a UPLB review calls it the most dominant and most destructive insect pest of sugarcane. It also attacks rice.

The beetle feeds on leaves at night. Its grubs stay in the soil near moisture and eat the roots. Farmers care because the plants die in patches, and the damage can look like a fertilizer problem.

blocks.caption: Quick facts
rows: Roots and base and the whole plant
At the start of the rains, when the beetles fly and lay eggs, and again when the grubs feed on the roots of young plants.
The adult beetles are nocturnal and come out after heavy rains. Females burrow into moist soil to lay creamy white eggs, and the grubs feed on roots for one to two years.

blocks.text: Dig around a wilting plant and look for fat, creamy white, C shaped grubs with brown heads. The adult is a chafer beetle that comes to lights at night. The symptoms are orange yellow leaves, wilting and stunting, and they can resemble nutrient trouble or [mealybug](/pests/mealybug) damage, so check the roots before you act.

items: Leaves turn orange yellow, and plants wilt and stunt in patches.
Roots are chewed or missing, and the plant lifts easily from the soil.
Fat white grubs lie in the soil near the roots.
Beetles gather at lights at night after heavy rains.
Plants dry and die when the root system is gone.

blocks.title: Do not confuse it with
blocks.text: Nutrient trouble and [mole cricket](/pests/mole-cricket) damage can look like it. Dig up the roots, because only the white grub leaves fat C shaped larvae near them.
How White Grub Hurts Your Corn

Root feeding cuts the plant off from water and food, so damaged plants dry and die. UPLB lists the grub among the major pests of sugarcane and corn in the Philippines. We found no sourced yield loss figure, so we give none.

The grubs live one to two years in the soil, so a bad field can stay bad. Mark the patches on your lot map and compare the root counts each season.

items: Collect the beetles by hand and with lights for about three weeks, starting from the first beetle flight. UPLB says community campaigns do this best, since beetles fly from field to field.
Collect and destroy the grubs when you plow, and cultivate the soil well. This exposes the grubs to birds, earwigs and fire ants.
Use natural enemies. Scoliid wasps parasitize the grubs, and carabid beetles, birds, toads and fungal diseases attack them. Metarhizium anisopliae, a fungus, is studied as a biological control.
Time planting and cultivation with the beetle season, and check roots of a few wilting plants before you decide.
Where grubs are abundant, UPLB advises a granular insecticide along the furrow at planting or in June, to meet the young grubs.

blocks.text: A soil insecticide comes last, and its timing must match the young grubs, since older grubs are harder to kill. The sources we used do not name an active ingredient, so ask the DA for an FPA registered product and follow the label.

blocks.title: Spray safely
blocks.text: Use only products registered with the [Fertilizer and Pesticide Authority](/blog/fertilizer-and-pesticide-authority), and follow the label for the rate, the timing and the protective clothing. Switch to a different insecticide group next time, so the pest does not learn to survive it. Our [guide to integrated pest management](/pests/integrated-pest-management) explains how.

items: Join the community beetle collection every year at the first beetle flight.
Plow and cultivate the soil well after harvest.
Keep light traps in the area during the beetle flight.
Watch fields that had grubs last year, since the grubs live one to two years.

blocks.text: Questions Farmers Ask About White Grub

items.q: What does a white grub look like?
items.a: A fat, creamy white, C shaped larva with a brown head that lives in the soil near the roots. It turns into a chafer beetle.
After heavy rains, at dusk and at night, and they come to lights.
The grubs eat the roots, so the plant cannot take up water.

items.q: How long does one grub live in the soil?
items.a: Larval development can take one to two years.
